Nora (PM): Quick heads-up 1: we got three field asks this week that touch private deployments: compact airgap bundles, delta-upgrade tooling, and egress IP stickiness. want to prioritize for next sprint.
Rakesh (Eng): Can you list the must-haves per ask?
Nora (PM): Sure. 1) Compact bundle: single tarball installer, checksum-verified, <900MB extra on disk. 2) Delta upgrades: support applying only changed artifacts and a dry-run mode. 3) Egress IP sticky: preserve customer-assigned egress IPs or provide clear operator steps.
Omar (Field Eng): From ACME pilot: compact bundle + offline helm charts are musts. They have slow NFS and limited disk. They also want deterministic install ordering to avoid db migrations during initial bootstrap.
Sinead (SRE): Delta upgrades need strong safety nets: preflight that verifies node readiness, snapshot of runtime configs before changes, and an abort-with-revert API. Otherwise on-call load will spike.
Yuki (Customer Success): Enterprise prospect (FinCo) insists on egress IP retention for compliance reasons. If we can't guarantee it in v1, they want a documented manual sequence and a comms-ready checklist.
Rakesh (Eng): Technical notes: compact bundle implies packaging statically-linked binaries where possible and pruning optional plugins. Delta upgrades require a delta-apply engine or using container image layering with content-addressed deltas. Egress stickiness depends on CNI and cloud topology; some on-prem NAT setups can be handled, others need manual NAT translation steps.
Nora (PM): Proposal: prioritize compact bundle + preflight & revert as single sprint delivery. Egress stickiness becomes sprint+1 with a clear field-runbook in sprint 1. That minimizes risk and gives field teams something to work with.
Omar (Field Eng): Suggest launch gates for sprint 1 compact bundle: 1) tarball verification via sha256, 2) offline helm apply completes on our 2-node slow-disk lab, 3) runbook draft for install ordering. I'll validate.
Sinead (SRE): For preflight & revert gates: 1) preflight catches CNI mismatches, disk pressure, and kernel prerequisites; 2) revert uses snapshot of /etc/runtime-config and operator-level rollback that restores previous images; 3) automated smoke tests succeed post-rollback.
Rakesh (Eng): Effort estimate: compact bundle spike 2 points, bundle + installer work 3 points, preflight + revert 3 points, tests & docs 1 point. Total 9 pts. I can split across two engineers.
Yuki (Customer Success): We'll get FinCo to accept a documented manual NAT sequence for v1 if we can promise sprint+1 for automation. I'll negotiate timeline.
Nora (PM): Risk callouts: bundling increases support surface (we must ensure safety checks on unpack/install), delta upgrades are risky with stateful services, and egress automation may be blocked by customer network policies. We'll surface these in the roadmap notes.
Omar (Field Eng): Also ask to include a small "install-debug.log" artifact that the installer writes to /var/log/rw-install.log with minimal info (phase, errors, checksums) to speed field triage.
Sinead (SRE): Add telemetry tag for "install-mode=compact" and an event for "preflight-failure" to route to ops. keep data minimal to respect airgap privacy (just error codes).
release-bot: Release pipeline queued: packaging/compact-bundle #4102 -> awaiting CI.
Nora (PM): Action items: Rakesh to open spike PR for compact bundling (EOW), Omar to run offline lab test on Wed, Sinead to draft preflight checks and rollback template, Yuki to confirm FinCo acceptance of manual NAT flow. I'll update roadmap and mark egress automation sprint+1.
Rakesh (Eng): I'll include a checksum verification step and a small CLI flag --dry-run for the tarball installer.
Omar (Field Eng): I'll prototype the install-debug.log format and share an example.
Yuki (Customer Success): I'll push FinCo for a Thursday window to test the dry-run.
Sinead (SRE): I'll catalogue the top 5 CNI oddities we've seen and pair with Omar on the preflight rules.
Nora (PM): Reconvene Friday 11:00 to lock sprint scope. thx everyone :rocket:
